## Generation method

Composite PNG was generated via Python/PIL direct sprite-sheet extraction — not a browser screenshot. Each frame is cropped at pixel-exact coordinates from the actual on-disk sprite sheets, then scaled with nearest-neighbor (pixel-art fidelity) at each scale factor. This is equivalent to the frame extraction logic in `src/scale-strip.ts` (`monsterTexture()` / `charTexture()`) — same layout-branch logic, same frame-0 extraction rule. No WebGL renderer involved.

## Per-row rendering anomalies and notes

**Goblin Mage (trash, 96×96, strip layout)**
No anomalies. Separate idle sheet used (not combined). 12 frames at 96px each in a horizontal strip; frame 0 extracted at x=0, y=0. Idle animation is clearly a standing pose.

**Mutant Skeleton (trash, 120×120, combined layout)**
Single combined sheet containing all animations. Frame 0 of combined sheet extracted. The idle pose appears to be near the start of the combined sheet — visible skeleton standing figure at all three scales.

**Evil Eye (trash, 64×64, combined layout)**
Smallest intrinsic frame in the roster. At scale 0.20 the rendered sprite is only 13px tall. The sprite occupies the full frame with a circular floating eye design. At 0.20 the sprite is very small; at 0.35 it's 22px. Flagged as a potential scale concern: even at the highest tested scale (0.35) the Evil Eye is substantially smaller than the player reference (22px vs 45px). Legolas intrinsic-size data may help determine whether the frame has meaningful empty margin — if the actual body occupies ~80% of the 64×64 frame, the effective body height at 0.35 is ~17px, which is very small.

**Sword Warrior (trash, 280×280, combined layout)**
Largest frame in the roster and a trash-tier outlier. At scale 0.35 it renders at 98px — larger than all elite, mini_boss, AND boss tier monsters except God of Lightning (90px). At scale 0.20 it's 56px, still larger than boss tier Angel Guardian at 0.20 (38px). This is a significant tier-size inversion: a trash mob rendered larger than bosses at the same scale. Recommend gandalf flag this for per-slug scale adjustment — Sword Warrior likely needs a lower per-slug scale if global scale is tuned upward for small-frame monsters.

**Crystal Golem (elite, 168×141, combined layout)**
Non-square frame (wider than tall). Frame 0 of combined sheet. Golem renders with a compact body; 141px frame height gives 28-49px range across scales. Reasonable sizing relative to other elites.

**Fire Elemental (elite, 192×68, combined layout)**
Very short frame (68px height vs 192px width). The elemental sprite is wide but short — it appears as a horizontal flame/ember shape. At scale 0.35, only 24px tall. Like Evil Eye, this sprite may appear undersized relative to player reference and other monsters. The wide-but-short frame shape means horizontal presence is not captured by the height metric. Recommend gandalf note this when evaluating: the elemental may feel "right-sized" horizontally even if the height number looks small.

**Demon Mage (elite, 192×128, row_per_anim layout)**
Layout is `row_per_anim` in metadata with no `row_index` field set on the single "combined" animation entry. The frame extraction defaults to row_index=0 (y=0), which extracts from the first row of the combined sheet. This behavior matches the existing `monsterTexture()` TypeScript function. The rendered sprite appears to show a mage character in what may be an attack frame rather than a strict idle — the combined sheet's row 0 may not be the idle animation row. Flagged: if gandalf needs true idle isolation for Demon Mage, legolas may need to add per-animation row_index metadata to the combined sheet.

**Lich (mini_boss, 176×128, grid layout)**
Separate idle sheet used (`sheets/idle.png`). Grid layout: sheet is 1408×256, containing 8 cols × 2 rows of 176×128 frames. Frame 0 extracted at x=0, y=0. Clear idle standing pose. Good reference for what a "proper idle frame" looks like vs combined-sheet frame 0 extraction.

**Hellfire Rhino (mini_boss, 234×112, combined layout)**
Wide, relatively short frame (234×112). Rhino sprite shows a large quadruped — the wide frame captures the full body width. Height-wise, at 0.35 it's 39px (shorter than player reference 45px despite being mini_boss tier). The rhino's bulk is more horizontal than vertical; height metric undersells its apparent visual size in-game.

**Angel Guardian (boss, 256×192, combined layout)**
Boss tier, 256×192 frame. At 0.35: 67px rendered height. This is the more "humanoid" of the two bosses — vertical stance. 67px vs player reference 45px means at scale 0.35 it renders ~49% taller than the player, which may be appropriate for a boss.

**God of Lightning (boss, 256×256, combined layout)**
Largest square frame (256×256). At 0.35: 90px rendered height. At 0.28: 72px. This is 2× the player reference height at 0.35 — strong visual presence. The square frame suggests the sprite fills width and height roughly equally. The combined sheet first frame appears to show a dramatic pose.

## Sizing concerns summary for gandalf

The following monsters are flagged as having notable scale concerns relative to the player reference (Fire Knight @ 45px at scale 0.35):

1. **Evil Eye (trash)** — 22px at 0.35 → only 49% of player height. Very small. Even raising to 0.35 may not give adequate visual presence. Consider per-slug scale candidate above 0.35 or verify with legolas whether the 64×64 frame has significant empty margin.

2. **Fire Elemental (elite)** — 24px at 0.35 → 53% of player height. Short frame (68px) limits height at any reasonable scale. The horizontal extent is not captured by height metric — may warrant a "visual footprint" assessment rather than pure height comparison.

3. **Sword Warrior (trash)** — 98px at 0.35 → 218% of player height (largest in roster). Trash tier rendering larger than all bosses except God of Lightning is a tier-hierarchy concern. The 280×280 frame is by far the largest in the trash tier. Per-slug scale correction likely needed.

4. **Demon Mage (elite)** — Row 0 of combined sheet may not be an idle frame. If first-frame fidelity matters for in-game rendering, row_index metadata may need updating.
